title: The Upside-Down Gallery Prank
crime_description: All 18 paintings in the contemporary wing were turned precisely 180 degrees upside down without tripping alarms.

suspect.name: Balthazar McSnazz
suspect.quirk: Speaks in rhyming couplets, often with a touch of irony

dossier.text: Security footage shows the lights in the contemporary wing flickering between 10:45 PM and 10:50 PM.
The janitor on duty, Maria Rodriguez, reports that the east wing's motion sensors were disabled between 10:30 PM and 10:45 PM.
Forensic analysis reveals that the paint on 'Echoes in the Void' contains a microscopic scratch pattern matching the suspect's signature juggling pins.

truth_timeline.event: Balthazar McSnazz sneaks into the east wing through the ventilation shaft.
Balthazar McSnazz executes the micro-crime using a custom-made, high-precision turning device.
Balthazar McSnazz flees, dropping a juggling pin near the scene of the crime.

lie_plan.cover_story: I was at a private juggling club meeting at the time of the prank. I'm just a humble entertainer, not a vandal.

weak_points.claim: The motion sensors were perfectly functional during the entire time.
weak_points.planned_slip: Slip statement: 'I'm sure Maria just got her wires crossed.'

weak_points.claim: The lights in the contemporary wing were just experiencing a minor power surge.
weak_points.planned_slip: Slip statement: 'It's just a coincidence, I'm sure.'

weak_points.claim: I've never seen those juggling pins before in my life.
weak_points.planned_slip: Slip statement: 'Maybe someone else used them for a performance?'

solution_contradictions: Balthazar McSnazz claimed the motion sensors were fine which directly conflicts with fact-2.
Balthazar McSnazz claimed the lights were just experiencing a power surge which directly conflicts with fact-1.
